mainTopic: Cutting the skin, the corners of the head and beard, tattooing, and counting מלקות for repeated sins
overview: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי treats שריטה and גדידה as one prohibition. שמואל rules that cutting with a tool makes one חייב, because he follows רבי יוסי. רבי יוחנן corrects a ברייתא so that for עבודה זרה only cutting with a tool makes one חייב, matching the פסוק about the prophets of the בעל. Next the גמרא explains the משנה about the corners of the head and beard: רב ששת's gestures, רבי אליעזר's view that it is one לאו, and the two פסוקים that show only a razor counts. רבי אליעזר also includes tweezers and a plane, because he holds they count as shaving. A new משנה teaches that a tattoo needs both cutting and dye, and רבי שמעון requires the name of an עבודה זרה. The גמרא then discusses putting ashes on a wound and sorts out which teachings belong to רב מלכיא and which to רב מלכיו. Finally, a משנה teaches that a נזיר, or one wearing כלאים, gets מלקות for each act done after a separate warning.

steps.title: רבי יוסי treats incision and laceration as one prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי's position: שריטה and גדידה are one prohibition, and the word "למת" written by גדידה applies to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds that an incision and a laceration are one and the same, and it is written there, "for the dead."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question from just before this point about how רבי יוסי reads the פסוקים. It says he treats שריטה and גדידה as one prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוסי treats both as one law, the word "למת" in the גדידה פסוק already teaches that the prohibition is about cutting over the dead. That frees up the other wording in the שריטה פסוק to teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / he is of the opinion
An incision (a scratch or cut in the skin)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds:
an incision and a laceration are one,
and it is written there: "for the dead."
phrases.notes: דברים 14:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the earlier part of the sugya about רבי יוסי's reading of the פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the source by joining two prohibitions into one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוסי uses the word 'לנפש' to make one liable for each dead person, it seemed he had no source left to teach that cutting is forbidden only over the dead.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because שריטה and גדידה are one prohibition, "למת" written by גדידה covers both.

steps.title: שמואל: cutting with a tool makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a person who makes a שריטה using a tool is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: One who cuts an incision with a tool is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new rule: a שריטה made with a tool, like a knife, still counts and the person is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might have thought שריטה only means scratching with your fingernails. שמואל says a tool counts too, and this sets up the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One who cuts an incision with a tool is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related new topic: how a שריטה is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שריטה made with a tool makes one חייב.

steps.title: A ברייתא says incision is by hand and laceration by tool
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says שריטה is done by hand and גדידה is done with a tool, which seems to go against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: An incision and a laceration are one, except that an incision is by hand and a laceration is with a tool!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a שריטה is made by hand, not with a tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a שריטה is by definition done by hand, then cutting with a tool is not a שריטה at all. That contradicts שמואל, who said a שריטה with a tool makes one חייב.

phrases.english: They challenged:
An incision and a laceration are one,
except that an incision is by hand
and a laceration is with a tool!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a שריטה with a tool makes one חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא defines שריטה as done by hand, so a cut made with a tool would not be a שריטה.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל holds like רבי יוסי, who treats שריטה and גדידה as completely the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: He spoke according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. He follows רבי יוסי, so the ברייתא's difference between hand and tool does not apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, שריטה and גדידה are fully one thing, so either one can be done by hand or by tool. The ברייתא follows a different view that does separate them.

keyTerms.meaning: He said it according to (the view of) ...

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל says a שריטה with a tool makes one חייב, because he holds like רבי יוסי that שריטה and גדידה are the same.

phrases.english: He spoke according to Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: "He" is שמואל, following רבי יוסי's view from the start of this section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ruling to a particular תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to go against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי יוסי, who treats the two as fully identical.

steps.title: A ברייתא on cutting for the dead and for idolatry
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites before רבי יוחנן: for a dead person, cutting by hand or by tool makes one חייב. For עבודה זרה, by hand one is חייב and by tool one is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רבי יוחנן: For a dead person, whether by hand or with a tool, he is liable. For idolatry, by hand he is liable; with a tool he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא recites a ברייתא in front of רבי יוחנן. It compares cutting for the dead with cutting for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the dead, the method does not matter. For עבודה זרה, the ברייתא as recited says only a cut by hand makes one חייב. The next step will question this.

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: This תנא is someone who memorized and recited ברייתות out loud for the sages.

phrases.aramaic: עַל מֵת, בֵּין בַּיָּד בֵּין בִּכְלִי – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: For a dead person, whether by hand or with a tool, he is liable;
for idolatry, by hand, he is liable;
with a tool, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on the same topic of hand versus tool.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the dead, both hand and tool make one חייב. For עבודה זרה, as first recited: hand makes one חייב, tool makes one פטור.

steps.title: The פסוק about Baal's priests shows the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects: the פסוק says idol worshippers cut themselves with swords and spears, so for עבודה זרה the usual way is with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the opposite is written: "And they cut themselves according to their custom with swords and spears"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges the ברייתא. A פסוק shows that idol worshippers cut themselves with tools, not by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "כמשפטם", "according to their custom", shows that tools were the normal way of cutting for עבודה זרה. So the ברייתא seems to have it backwards.

phrases.english: But the opposite is written:
"And they lacerated themselves according to their custom
with swords and spears"!
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:28, about the prophets of the בעל on הר הכרמל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the עבודה זרה half of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that for עבודה זרה only a cut by hand makes one חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows that idol worshippers' custom was to cut with tools, the opposite of the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן flips the ruling for idolatry
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן corrects the ברייתא: for עבודה זרה, by hand one is פטור and with a tool one is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: by hand, he is exempt; with a tool, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן fixes the wording of the ברייתא so that it matches the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since cutting for עבודה זרה was normally done with tools, that is the way that makes one חייב. Cutting by hand for עבודה זרה is not their usual way, so one is פטור. Cutting for the dead stays חייב either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (read the text this way)

steps.whatToRemember: For the dead: hand or tool, חייב. For עבודה זרה: with a tool, חייב; by hand, פטור.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not remember the ברייתא the way the תנא first recited it. רבי יוחנן reversed it, and the corrected version is the one that counts.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
by hand, he is exempt; with a tool, he is liable.
phrases.notes: This is only about cutting for עבודה זרה. The part about a dead person stays the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by changing the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For עבודה זרה, a cut by hand makes one חייב and a cut with a tool makes one פטור.
steps.terutzMaskana: For עבודה זרה, a cut with a tool makes one חייב and a cut by hand makes one פטור, matching the פסוק.

steps.title: רב ששת points to the corners of the head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about rounding the corners of the head, and says רב ששת would point to the spot between the parts of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he is liable for the head." רב ששת would point to between the parts of the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה about the corners of the head. It shows where they are by describing רב ששת's gesture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say exactly where the "corner" of the head is. רב ששת showed it by pointing to the place where the parts of the head meet, by the temples.

keyTerms.meaning: The joints or sections of the head

phrases.english: "And he is liable for the head."
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, about rounding off the corners of the head.

phrases.aramaic: מַחְוֵי רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בֵּין פִּירְקֵי רֵישָׁא.
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would point to between the parts of the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The corner of the head is at the place between the sections of the head, by the temples.

steps.title: רב ששת points to the five corners of the beard
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the beard has five corners: two on each side and one below. רב ששת would point to the spots between the sections of the beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And for the beard: two from here, two from there, and one from below." רב ששת would point to between the parts of the beard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the five corners of the beard and again describes רב ששת's gesture showing where they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה counts five corners of the beard. רב ששת showed their places by pointing to where the sections of the beard meet, at the joints of the jaw and chin.
steps.whatToRemember: The head has corners at the temples, and the beard has five corners. רב ששת pointed to exactly where they are.

phrases.english: "And for the beard,
two from here and two from there
and one from below."

phrases.aramaic: מַחְוֵי רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בֵּין פִּירְקֵי דִּיקְנָא.
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would point to between the parts of the beard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 8, now about the beard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beard's five corners are at the places between its sections: two on each side and one below.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר holds it is one prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר from the משנה and explains that he sees the beard corners as one single לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: If he removed them, etc. He holds that it is one prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's view from the משנה. It explains why he gives only one set of lashes for all five corners: he holds it is one לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים count each corner of the beard separately. רבי אליעזר holds the whole beard falls under one לאו, so removing all the corners at once gets only one set of lashes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If he removed them, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: if he removed all the corners in one act, he gets only one set of lashes.

phrases.english: He holds: it is one prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה about the five corners of the beard and explains רבי אליעזר's view on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, destroying the corners of the beard is one לאו, not five.

steps.title: Two verses show only a razor counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that one is חייב only with a razor, and brings a ברייתא proving it from the words 'shave' and 'destroy'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is not liable until he removes it with a razor. The חכמים taught: 'And the corner of their beard they shall not shave.' One might think that even if he shaved it with scissors he would be liable. So the פסוק says: 'You shall not destroy.' If it said only 'You shall not destroy,' one might think that if he removed it with tweezers or a plane he would be liable. So the פסוק says: 'They shall not shave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that only a razor makes one חייב. Then it brings a ברייתא that uses two פסוקים to show where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Shave' alone could include scissors, so 'destroy' teaches that the hair must be destroyed from the root. 'Destroy' alone could include tweezers or a plane, so 'shave' teaches that it must be a real shaving act. Each word limits the other.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall not destroy (the corner of your beard)
Tweezers and a plane, tools that pull or scrape hair off
The verse teaches (to stop a wrong idea)

phrases.english: And he is not liable until he removes it with a razor.
The Rabbis taught:
"And the corner of their beard they shall not shave,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:5

phrases.english: one might think that even if he shaved it with scissors
he would be liable?
The verse teaches: "You shall not destroy."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:27

phrases.english: If it said only "You shall not destroy,"
one might think that if he removed it with tweezers or a plane
he would be liable?
The verse teaches: "They shall not shave."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וּפְאַת זְקָנָם לֹא יְגַלֵּחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה, about which tool makes one חייב, and gives its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two פסוקים, 'shave' and 'destroy', each limit the other, so only certain tools count.

steps.title: The answer is a razor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the only tool that both shaves and destroys is a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Shaving that includes destroying — you must say this is a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא puts the two פסוקים together and gives its final answer: only a razor makes one חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We need a tool that is both 'shaving' and 'destroying' at once. Scissors shave but do not destroy, and tweezers destroy but do not shave. Only a razor does both.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (how do the two verses fit together)

steps.whatToRemember: For the חכמים, only a razor makes one חייב for the beard corners, because only a razor both 'shaves' and 'destroys'.

phrases.english: How so?
Shaving that includes destroying —
you must say this is a razor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two limits from step 11 into one final rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only a razor counts, since it is both shaving and destroying.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי אליעזר about tweezers and scissors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר, who makes one חייב even with tweezers or a plane, and shows his view seems not to work either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Even if he removed it with tweezers or a plane he would be liable. Whichever way you take it: If he learns the גזירה שוה, he should require a razor. If he does not learn the גזירה שוה, then scissors too should not be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's view and then attacks it. It shows that his view does not fit with either possible way of learning the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר links the two פסוקים through a גזירה שוה, he should agree with the חכמים that only a razor counts. If he does not link them, there is no reason to exempt scissors either. Either way, his view of including tweezers but exempting scissors seems hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you take it (a two-sided challenge)
A link between two פסוקים that share a similar word

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying which side רבי אליעזר holds. It is saying that both sides cause a problem for him. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Even if he removed it with tweezers or a plane
he would be liable.
Whichever way you take it:
If he learns the verbal link —
phrases.notes: This links 'shave' in the כהנים verse with 'destroy' in the verse for everyone, just like the ברייתא did.

phrases.english: he should require a razor;
if he does not learn the verbal link —
then scissors too should not be exempt!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets comes from the corrected wording, so read it as: he shouldn't exempt scissors either.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נַפְשָׁךְ: אִי גְּמִיר גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the חכמים' razor rule to challenge רבי אליעזר's wider rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that tweezers and a plane make one חייב while scissors do not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma: with the גזירה שוה only a razor should count; without it, scissors should count too. Neither option matches his view.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר counts tweezers and a plane as shaving
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר does learn from the גזרה שוה, but he holds that tweezers and a plane also count as shaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he does learn the גזרה שוה. He simply holds that these tools (tweezers and a plane) also shave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from step 13 about how רבי אליעזר can make one חייב with tweezers or a plane.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר agrees with the חכמים about the source: the tool must both 'shave' and 'destroy'. He only argues about what counts as shaving. In his view tweezers and a plane also shave, so they fit the rule too.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (the גמרא keeps its first idea)
A link between two פסוקים that use the same word

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים is only about what counts as shaving, not about the source.

phrases.english: Actually, he does learn the verbal analogy,
phrases.notes: This is the 'shave' and 'destroy' link from the ברייתא in step 11.

phrases.english: and he holds: these too do shaving.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the tweezers and the plane.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: the argument is about what counts as shaving
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר seemed to either reject the גזרה שוה or contradict it
steps.terutzMaskana: He accepts the גזרה שוה and holds that tweezers and a plane also shave

steps.title: משנה: a tattoo needs both cutting and dye
steps.stepSummary: One is חייב for a כתובת קעקע only if he both cuts the skin and puts in dye or anything that leaves a mark.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who makes a tattoo. If he wrote (put in dye) but did not cut, or cut but did not write, he is not חייב. He is חייב only once he writes and cuts, with ink, with kohl, or with anything that leaves a mark.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new לאו: tattooing. It says what counts as a full tattoo.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tattoo has two parts: cutting into the skin and putting color into the cut. Doing only one part is not enough for מלקות. Any material that leaves a lasting mark counts, not just ink.

keyTerms.meaning: He cut / carved into the skin

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who writes a tattoo inscription.
If he wrote but did not carve,
phrases.notes: 'Writing' is putting in the dye; 'carving' is cutting into the skin.

phrases.english: or carved but did not write, he is not liable,
until he writes and carves,
with ink and with kohl,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'with his hand' (in round brackets); the corrected wording, in square brackets, says 'with ink'.

phrases.english: and with anything that leaves a mark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new לאו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One is חייב for tattooing only when he both cuts the skin and puts in a marking substance

steps.title: רבי שמעון: liable only for writing 'the name'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יהודה, in the name of רבי שמעון, says one is חייב only if he writes 'the name', based on the words 'אני ה׳' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: He is not חייב until he writes the name there, as it says: 'And a tattoo you shall not put on yourselves, I am ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second opinion that adds a condition: the tattoo must be of a 'name'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learns from the end of the פסוק, 'אני ה׳', that the איסור is about writing a name. The משנה does not say which name; the גמרא will explain this next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The name' (which name is explained in the גמרא)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיִּכְתּוֹב שָׁם אֶת הַשֵּׁם,
phrases.english: He is not liable until he writes the name there,
as it is stated: “And a tattoo inscription you shall not place upon you,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:28

phrases.english: I am the Lord.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion in the same משנה, adding a condition
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One is חייב only if the tattoo is of 'the name'

steps.title: Must he actually write the words 'I am the Lord'?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי whether רבי שמעון means one must literally tattoo the words 'אני ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: Does he mean only if he writes 'אני ה׳' itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking what 'the name' in רבי שמעון's view means. This sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי שמעון brought the words 'אני ה׳' as his source, one could read him as saying the tattoo must be those exact words. רב אחא asks if that is really what he means.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
Is it only once he writes “I am the Lord” itself?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רבי שמעון's 'name' means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'the name' means literally the words 'אני ה׳'

steps.title: It means the name of an idol
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers no: as בר קפרא taught, one is חייב only for tattooing the name of an עבודה זרה, since 'אני ה׳' means 'I am ה׳ and no other'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. As בר קפרא taught: He is not חייב until he writes the name of an עבודה זרה, as it says, 'And a tattoo you shall not put on yourselves, I am ה׳' — I am ה׳, and no other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question: 'the name' is the name of an idol, not the words 'אני ה׳'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אני ה׳' are read as a warning: only ה׳ is God, so do not mark yourself with the name of another god. This turns רבי שמעון's source into a reason, not the text of the tattoo.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, the tattoo איסור with מלקות is about the name of an עבודה זרה: 'I am ה׳, and no other.'

phrases.english: He said to him: No.
Rather, as bar Kappara teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיִּכְתּוֹב שֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: He is not liable until he writes the name of an idol,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּכְתוֹבֶת קַעֲקַע לֹא תִתְּנוּ בָּכֶם אֲנִי ה׳״ –
phrases.english: as it is stated: “And a tattoo inscription you shall not place upon you, I am the Lord,”
meaning: I am the Lord, and no other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא. כִּדְתָנֵי בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The name' is the name of an עבודה זרה; 'אני ה׳' means no other god

steps.title: No ashes on a wound, because it looks like a tattoo
steps.stepSummary: רב מלכיא in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה forbids putting burnt ashes on a wound, because it looks like a כתובת קעקע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מלכיא said in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה: A person may not put burnt ashes on his wound, because it looks like a tattoo.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related rule: something that only looks like a tattoo is also forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes on an open wound leave a dark mark in the skin that looks like a tattoo. Even though it is not a real tattoo, it is forbidden because of how it looks.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מַלְכִּיָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Malkiyya says that Rav Adda bar Ahava says:
It is forbidden for a person to put
burnt ashes on his wound,
because it looks like a tattoo.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַלְכִּיָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the tattoo topic to something that only looks like one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting burnt ashes on a wound is forbidden because it looks like a tattoo

steps.title: A memory list: which rulings belong to which rabbi
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בריה דרב איקא gives a list: skewer, maidservants and hair pits are from רב מלכיו; forelock, burnt ashes and cheese are from רב מלכיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן, son of רב איקא, said: Skewer, maidservants and pits are רב מלכיו's. Forelock, burnt ashes and cheese are רב מלכיא's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to give a memory list so we know which rulings were said by רב מלכיו and which by רב מלכיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rabbis quoted רב אדא בר אהבה and have almost the same name, so their rulings were easy to mix up. Each key word stands for one ruling, and the ruling about ashes from step 19 is placed under רב מלכיא.
steps.confusionAlert: רב מלכיא and רב מלכיו are two different rabbis with almost the same name. Read the endings carefully: ־יָּא versus ־יּוֹ.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling about ashes on a wound belongs to רב מלכיא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman, son of Rav Ika, says:
Skewer, maidservants and pits are Rav Malkiyyu's,
phrases.notes: Each word is a short tag for a whole ruling, just to help you remember who said what.

phrases.aramaic: בְּלוֹרִית, אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה וּגְבִינָה – רַב מַלְכִּיָּא
phrases.english: forelock, burnt ashes and cheese are Rav Malkiyya's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sorts out who said the ruling of step 19 and related rulings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory list giving each set of rulings to the right rabbi

steps.title: רב פפא's rule for telling רב מלכיא and רב מלכיו apart
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says teachings tied to a משנה or ברייתא come from רב מלכיא, and stand-alone teachings come from רב מלכיו. He gives a memory sign: 'the משנה is a queen.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: Teachings about a משנה or a ברייתא are from רב מלכיא. Independent teachings are from רב מלכיו. Your memory sign: 'The משנה is a queen (מלכתא).'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a different way to sort which teachings belong to רב מלכיא and which belong to רב מלכיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, רב נחמן בריה דרב איקא sorted the teachings by giving a list. רב פפא sorts them by type instead. Comments on a משנה or ברייתא go to רב מלכיא, and stand-alone rulings (שמעתתא) go to רב מלכיו.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים left out of the משנה
Stand-alone halachic teachings of the אמוראים

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
Teachings on a mishnah or a baraita are from Rav Malkiyya;
independent halachic teachings are from Rav Malkiyyu.
And your memory sign: the mishnah is a queen.
phrases.notes: מלכתא (queen) sounds like מלכיא, so you link the משנה with רב מלכיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different rule from the list רב נחמן בריה דרב איקא gave in step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teachings tied to a משנה or ברייתא are from רב מלכיא; stand-alone teachings are from רב מלכיו.

steps.title: What difference is there between the two rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רב נחמן's list and רב פפא's rule would actually give different answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two ways of sorting the teachings ever lead to a different result. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rules seem to sort the teachings in a similar way. The גמרא wants to find a specific teaching that the two rules would assign to different people.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means רב נחמן's list from step 20 and רב פפא's rule from step 21.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רב פפא's rule differs in practice from רב נחמן's list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which teaching would be credited to a different person under each rule

steps.title: They differ about the ruling on maidservants
steps.stepSummary: The two rules disagree about who said the ruling on maidservants.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the ruling about maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two rules split over the teaching about maidservants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's list credited the maidservants ruling to רב מלכיו. That ruling relates to a משנה, so under רב פפא's rule it belongs to רב מלכיא.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: The difference between them is the ruling about maidservants.
phrases.notes: This ruling is about a משנה, so רב פפא would credit it to רב מלכיא, not רב מלכיו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The maidservants ruling is credited to רב מלכיו by רב נחמן but to רב מלכיא by רב פפא.
steps.whatToRemember: Both rules agree on almost everything. They differ only about the maidservants ruling.

steps.title: רב ביבי was strict even about a bloodletting wound
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי would not put ashes even on the small wound left from bloodletting, because it might look like a כתובת קעקע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי was strict even about the wound of bloodletting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב מלכיא's ruling against putting burnt ashes on a wound (step 19). It tells us רב ביבי בר אביי was strict about this even for a bloodletting wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think a small bloodletting cut is too minor to count. רב ביבי still avoided putting ashes on it, because even this could look like a כתובת קעקע.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye was strict
phrases.notes: He means strict about not putting burnt ashes on a wound, the ruling from step 19.

phrases.english: even about the wound of bloodletting.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי קָפֵיד אֲפִילּוּ אַרִיבְדָּא דְּכוּסִילְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ruling about burnt ashes on a wound from step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not put ashes even on a bloodletting wound.

steps.title: רב אשי: the wound itself shows the ashes are for healing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that wherever there is a wound, the wound shows that the ashes are there to heal, not to make a tattoo.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: Any place where there is a wound, his wound proves it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes a more lenient view than רב ביבי. If there is a real wound, putting ashes on it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that ashes in the skin look like a כתובת קעקע. רב אשי says people can see the wound, so they will understand the ashes are medicine, not a tattoo.

keyTerms.meaning: Proves about it / shows the reason

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:
Any place where there is a wound,
his wound proves it for him.
phrases.notes: Everyone can see the ashes are there to heal the wound, so it doesn't look like a tattoo.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more lenient view than רב ביבי's strictness
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ashes on a real wound are allowed, because the wound shows they are for healing.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ביבי was strict even about a bloodletting wound. רב אשי says a visible wound makes it clear the ashes are only medicine.

steps.title: A נזיר drinking wine: one set of lashes, or one for each warning
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a נזיר who drinks wine all day gets only one set of מלקות. If he is warned again and again and drinks after each warning, he gets מלקות for each drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A נזיר who was drinking wine all day is liable for only one set of lashes. If they said to him 'Do not drink, do not drink,' and he drinks, he is liable for each and every time.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that what decides the number of מלקות is the number of separate warnings, not the number of sips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinking all day after one warning counts as one sin, so he gets one set of מלקות. Each new warning (התראה) followed by another drink makes a new sin, so each one gets its own מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, the start of a משנה
A person who took a vow not to drink wine, not to become impure from the dead, and not to cut his hair
Liable for each and every one

steps.confusionAlert: 'Only one' does not mean he drank only once. He may have drunk many times. Without new warnings, it all counts as one sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for counting מלקות: each new warning followed by a new act counts as a new sin.

phrases.english: Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן כׇּל הַיּוֹם –
phrases.english: A nazir who was drinking wine all day
is liable for only one set of lashes.
If they said to him, 'Do not drink! Do not drink!'
and he drinks,
he is liable for each and every time.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן כׇּל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on counting מלקות for repeated sins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One warning means one set of מלקות, however many times he drinks. Repeated warnings, each followed by a drink, mean מלקות for each one.

steps.title: A נזיר becoming impure from the dead follows the same rule
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who becomes טמא from dead bodies all day gets one set of מלקות. If he is warned each time and does it again, he gets מלקות for each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was making himself impure to the dead all day, he is liable only once. If they said to him 'Do not become impure, do not become impure,' and he becomes impure, he is liable for each and every time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same rule to a second נזיר prohibition: becoming impure from the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of מלקות again depends on separate warnings. One warning covers a whole day of becoming impure; each new warning and new act adds another set of מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Making himself impure through contact with the dead

phrases.english: If he was making himself impure to the dead all day,
he is liable only once.
If they said to him, 'Do not become impure! Do not become impure!'
and he becomes impure,
he is liable for each and every time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of step 26 to the נזיר's ban on becoming impure from the dead
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Becoming impure all day after one warning is one sin; each new warning and new act is another sin.

steps.title: A נזיר shaving follows the same rule
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who shaves all day gets one set of מלקות. If he is warned each time and shaves again, he gets מלקות for each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was shaving all day, he is liable only once. If they said to him 'Do not shave, do not shave,' and he shaves, he is liable for each and every time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same rule to the third נזיר prohibition: cutting his hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three things forbidden to a נזיר (wine, impurity from the dead, and shaving) follow one pattern. One warning means one set of מלקות, and repeated warnings with repeated acts mean many.

phrases.english: If he was shaving all day,
he is liable only once.
If they said to him, 'Do not shave! Do not shave!'
and he shaves,
he is liable for each and every time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same rule to the נזיר's ban on shaving
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shaving all day after one warning is one sin; each new warning and new shave is another sin.

steps.title: Wearing כלאים: one set of lashes, or one for each time he puts it back on
steps.stepSummary: Someone who wears a garment of כלאים all day gets one set of מלקות. If he is warned each time, and he takes it off and puts it on again, he gets מלקות for each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was wearing כלאים all day, he is liable only once. If they said to him 'Do not wear it, do not wear it,' and he takes it off and puts it on, he is liable for each and every time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from נזיר to a different prohibition, כלאים in clothing, and applies the same counting rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of the משנה, he takes the garment off and puts it on again after each warning, which is a new act of wearing. Each new putting-on after a warning brings its own מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden mixture; here, a garment of wool and linen together (שעטנז)

phrases.english: If he was wearing kilayim all day,
he is liable only once.
If they said to him, 'Do not wear it! Do not wear it!'
and he takes it off and puts it on,
he is liable for each and every time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same counting rule to wearing כלאים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wearing כלאים all day is one sin. Each time he takes it off and puts it back on after a new warning is another sin.
steps.whatToRemember: In every case in this משנה, the number of מלקות depends on separate warnings, each followed by a new act. Doing the same thing all day after one warning counts as only one sin.
